source_documents.title: Intramolecular Photoinduced Charge Transfer and Recombination Dynamics in Vinylarene Terminated Organosilanes

reference_evidence_units.quote: the latter is the optically induced intramolecular charge transfer transition that results from combining the silane donor and arene acceptor.
reference_evidence_units.subject: organosilanes
reference_evidence_units.statement: A σ→π* CT absorption band exists only in the silane-arene hybrids.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: From earlier work by the group; red-edge trend measured here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: which populates the emissive charge-separated state
reference_evidence_units.subject: organosilanes
reference_evidence_units.statement: The σ→π* transition directly populates the emissive CT state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: All structures exhibit similar photoinduced ultrafast spectral dynamics that we ascribe to relaxation of the nascent charge-separated excited state followed by a return to the ground state via charge recombination.
reference_evidence_units.subject: organosilanes

reference_evidence_units.quote: weak acceptors produce charge-separated states that exhibit relatively large electronic coupling for back-electron transfer (approaching the adiabatic limit) that result in fast recombination
reference_evidence_units.subject: organosilanes
reference_evidence_units.statement: Recombination analysed as back-electron transfer; acceptor strength sets coupling.

reference_evidence_units.quote: stimulated emission band appears instantaneously for Si2s-2C
reference_evidence_units.subject: Si2s-2C
reference_evidence_units.statement: Prompt stimulated emission from the CT state (recombination ~237 ps in DCM).

reference_evidence_units.quote: we do not see an enhancement in the charge-recombination lifetime for Si2s-2C
reference_evidence_units.subject: Si2s-2C
reference_evidence_units.statement: Faster recombination in cyclohexane from larger coupling.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Si2s-2C: direct σ→π* excitation of the σ-π conjugated silane donor / vinylarene acceptor populates the emissive CT state (guideline §3.3: CT state of a conjugated D-A system → ICT).

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The nonradiative return of the CT state is analysed as back-electron transfer (electronic coupling, Marcus inverted regime).

contrast_group.varied_factor: acceptor strength (dicyanovinyl 2C vs diestervinyl 2E) at Si2; silane length (Si2 vs Si4) for 2C
contrast_group.paper_difference: Weak acceptors give strongly coupled CT states with fast recombination; longer silane lowers coupling.

reannotation.note: Previous PET primary changed to ICT primary: the CT state is reached by direct σ→π* optical CT excitation in a σ-π conjugated D-A system (guideline §3.3 boundary); recombination kept as PET secondary. Expert should check this boundary.
